By this award, claim petition under section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, would be
decided.

2.  The facts as stated in the claim petition are as under:- Deceased Pinku Pawar, Son of Petitioner No.1 and Petitioner No.2 and brother of Petitioner No.3, died on account of a motor accident, which occurred on 11.10.2019 at about 10:00 p.m., near Oriental Bank of Commerce Village Mandola, P.S.-
Tronica City, Ghaziabad, U.P.

sentences.text: was registered at PS Tronica City on 12.10.2019.

As per the claim petition,
at the relevant time, deceased was going to his house alongwith his cousin Suraj on his motorcycle bearing Registration No. UP-17N-8387 as a pillion rider with due precaution and care and when they reached near OBC Bank, Village Mandola, P.S. Tronica City, U.P., at the same time, the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Registration No.HR-55AA-4292 which was coming from back side,
hit the deceased's vehicle with great force.
The driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle rashly, negligently and at a very high speed.
As a result of this, the deceased fell down on the road alongwith his cousin and vehicle and received fatal injuries as per the post mortem report.

Deceased was shifted to MMG Hospital, Ghaziabad, U.P., where doctors examined him and declared him dead and post mortem was conducted by the doctors of MMG Hospital, U.P.
3.
On service of notice of the petition, all the three respondents marked appearance and filed their written statements.
Respondent No.1 & Respondent No.2 filed joint written statement mentioning that the vehicle of R2 has not caused any accident as alleged by the petitioner.
It is further submitted that the alleged offending vehicle is duly insured with R3/Universal Sompo GIC Ltd. & R1 was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.

The insurance company/ Respondent No.3 has filed its written statement separately and it is specifically stated in the written statement that the accident occurred due to the driving in negligent manner by the deceased himself and not due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the alleged vehicle.
It is further submitted that amount of compensation claimed is very high and exorbitant.
It is further submitted that there is unexplained delay of 01 day in filing of FIR and injured was travelling with two other pillion riders and hence violating the traffic rules.
Other general defences have been taken by R3/Insurer.

4. On the basis of pleadings, following issues were framed on 28.08.2018 :-
(i) Whether Mr. Pinku Pawar died in a motor vehicular accident, which happened on 11.10.2019 at about 10:00 p.m. near Oriental Bank of Commerce, Village Mandola,
within the jurisdiction of PS Tronica City, Ghaziabad, U.P., due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing Registration No. HR-55AA-4292 driven by the Respondent No. 1 / Akram?

5(i).

Petitioner No.1 Ms. Kamlesh (PW1), herself stepped into the witness box and relied upon affidavit Ex.PW1/A, deposed about the manner of accident and relied upon the following documents:
(i) Copy of Aadhar Card and PAN Card of all of the Petitioners are Ex.PW1/A.

Certified copy of Criminal Case Record bearing Case No. 664 of 2019 pending before Ld. CJM, Ghaziabad is Ex.PW1/C. 5(ii).
PW2/Sh. Suraj Panwar has been further examined as an eye-witness to the accident and deposed regarding manner of accident.

Thereafter, PE was closed.
6. Respondent side did not choose to lead any evidence in their behalf and their opportunities to lead RE was closed on 24.07.2024.
7. I have heard Ms. Sulekha Thakur, Ld. Counsel for petitioners and Ms. Bhavna Sharma on behalf of main counsel Sh. S.K. Sharma, Ld. Counsel for R3/ insurer.
Record of the case has also been perused.
8. In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact, is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further, in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
9. In order to prove the case, petitioner examined two witnesses i.e. PW1 and PW2.

PW1 tendered her testimony by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/1 and deposed that on 11.10.2019, at about 10:00 P.M.,
her son/deceased was going home with his cousin on vehicle bearing No. UP-17N-8387 and when he reached near OBC Bank, Tronica City, U.P., driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.HR-55AA-4292 came from back side and hit the vehicle of the deceased while driving at high speed.
Deceased fell down on the road and received fatal injuries and was declared dead by the doctors in Government Hospital U.P.
She deposed that she was not an eye-witness of the accident.
PW2 Sh. Suraj Pawar also tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW2/1 and deposed regarding the manner of accident.
He clearly deposed that R1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed.
He further deposed that he had driving licence at the time of accident but he did not place on record his DL.
He further deposed that had called on 100 number but he did not file any GD Entry and he also did not know who had lodged the FIR.

The testimony of PW2 could not be shattered in his cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for R3.
10.
Respondent No.1 & Respondent No.2 i.e. Driver and Owner of the offending vehicle did not lead any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.

13. Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to the deceased victim Sh. Pinku Pawar.
Therefore, Issue No.1 is decided in favour of petitioners.
14. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
ASSESSMENT OF INCOME OF THE DECEASED:
15. PW1 is mother of the deceased and one of the claimants.
It has come in her evidence that deceased was her son and was doing a private job as a driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and he was sole bread earner of the family.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner submitted that deceased was unmarried at the time of accident and aged only 22 years.
PW1 had not filed on record any income and occupation proof of deceased.
No document in proof of age of the deceased is filed either in the shape of his birth certificate or educational record.
The copy of aadhar card of the deceased reflects his date of birth as 17.07.1997.
Petitioners have not made any averment or filed any documents in support of the educational qualification of the deceased.
No bank account statement of the deceased is filed either.
No driving licence of the deceased is proved on record to suggest that he was a driver by profession.
Perusal of cross-examination of PW1 shows that she has two daughters and one son and one of his daughters is already married.

She was given suggestion by Ld.
Counsel for R3 that deceased was not doing any private job as a driver or earning as claimed and further that he was not the sole earning member of his family.
From testimony of PW1, it comes to fore that the entire family is resident of Baghpat, U.P.
The aadhar card of the deceased shows him to be a resident of Baghpat, U.P.

In the absence of any income proof and education related proof of the deceased victim, his income has to be considered, being a resident of Uttar Pradesh, as per the minimum wages applicable to an unskilled worker on the date of accident i.e. 11.10.2019.
Hence, his income is considered to be Rs.8278/- per month.

sentences.text: The age of deceased was 22 years at the time of accident as per his Aadhar card Ex.PW1/B.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:-
 MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 &
 21 to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9
Age group between 56 to 60 yrs
M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5 Age group between 66 and above Therefore, the multiplier of 18 which is applicable for age group between 21 to 25 years shall be applicable in this case.

FUTURE PROSPECTS:
17.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age Kamlesh And Others vs Akram And Others on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77163412/
5 of 40 years.

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
18. The deceased can be presumed to be as self-employed.
Since the deceased Sh. Pinku Pawar was 22 years old, 40% future prospects has to be granted.
DEDUCTION TOWARDS PERSONAL LIVING EXPENSES:
19. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards her personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Married Persons Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six) Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Bachelor In case family is not large Half

entities.text: Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case dependents are the widowed 1/3rd mother and large number of younger non- earning sisters and brothers 20
. Petitioners are parents and unmarried sister of the deceased.
All petitioners are stated to be dependents of the deceased.
Sister of the deceased can be considered as primarily dependent on her father.
Family was not large and further, deceased was a bachelor, as per submissions of the Counsel for the petitioners.
Hence, 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

21. Thus, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.12,51,633.5/- (8278 x 1/2 x 140/100 x 12 x 18).
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
22.

In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-, 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.

21. Thus, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.12,51,633.5/- (8278 x 1/2 x 140/100 x 12 x 18).
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
22.
In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-, 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
In this case, there were five legal heirs of the deceased at the time of accident and filing of the claim petition.
Thus, all five claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- (48,000x3+18,000+18,000) under this head.
Petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization, except for the period for which the interest, if any, has been stopped by order of the Tribunal during inquiry.
LIABILITY 24.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company namely Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Ltd. has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and, in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/ insurance company becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
25. In view of above discussion, respondent No. 3/ insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
ISSUE No.3/RELIEF 26.
This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.14,32,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Thirty Two Thousands Only) to the petitioners along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.3/Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Ltd.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
27. The apportionment of the award amount shall be decided only after deposit of award amount.
28. With these observations, the claim petition is disposed of.

22.

In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-, 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
In this case, there were five legal heirs of the deceased at the time of accident and filing of the claim petition.
Thus, all five claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- (48,000x3+18,000+18,000) under this head.

Petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization, except for the period for which the interest, if any, has been stopped by order of the Tribunal during inquiry.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company namely Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Ltd. has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and, in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/ insurance company becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
25. In view of above discussion, respondent No. 3/ insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.14,32,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Thirty Two Thousands Only) to the petitioners along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.3/Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Ltd.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
27. The apportionment of the award amount shall be decided only after deposit of award amount.
28. With these observations, the claim petition is disposed of.
